traits.habitat_notes: Alkaline or saline soils of semiarid and arid plains, alkali flats and playa margins, dry washes and desert-shrub and sagebrush communities, often in pure stands where the water table is shallow (a phreatophyte), western North America from Alberta and Saskatchewan to Sonora, 600-2400 m.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form chosen from the plant's habit: a stiff, thorny desert shrub with pale branches standing out at wide angles and fleshy linear leaves.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species.

allometry.note: 2.58 m tall at 20 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a stiff, thorny desert shrub with pale branches standing out at wide angles and fleshy linear leaves.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): shrubs; Wikipedia: the wood is yellow, very hard and tough.

traits.life_span.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): a native flowering perennial.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): deciduous leaves; drops its leaves in fall and early winter.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): plants 1-2(-5) m; Wikipedia 0.5-3 m.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): to 5 m at the extreme; FEIS says to 3 m.

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): 3 to 6 feet (0.9-1.8 m) across.

traits.stem_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): stems erect; FEIS: erect to low and spreading.

traits.stem_clump.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): multiple brittle branches; may have several major stems arising from one large clump. 'Few' is our reading.

traits.clonal.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): clonal, with major stem clones arising from one large clump, sprouting from the root crown and lateral roots (though one Montana study found no vegetative reproduction).

traits.crown_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): divaricating shrubs, with elongate lateral branches and thorns from the main stems at more or less right angles, making a tangle of branches and thorns in mature plants; species: loosely and irregularly branched, proximal branches rarely touching the ground.

traits.spines.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): branches spinescent; the ends of smaller branches taper to sharp thorns. FNA: thorns 1(-2) per node.

traits.short_shoots.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): short shoots clustered, budlike, cushionlike, in the position of leaf scars.

traits.bark_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: grey to grey-brown older bark; FNA uses bark colour to tell the two species apart but does not state it; no source read names it.

traits.twig_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: young stems whitish to pale straw, as greasewood is usually pictured; no source read names it.

traits.stem_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): shrubs glabrous or pubescent; species leaves usually glabrous or slightly pubescent.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): leaves mostly solitary on elongate shoots of current season.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: solitary alternate leaves on long shoots in a spiral; FNA calls the staminate flowers spirally arranged but says nothing of leaves.

traits.leaf_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): blade somewhat flattened.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): blade linear.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): apex obtuse (mucronate).

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): margins entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): usually glabrous or slightly pubescent.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): blade (0.3-)1.5-4(-5) cm; FEIS 1-4 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: English Wikipedia, 'Sarcobatus' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): leaves 10-40 mm long and 1-2 mm broad.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): leaves sessile.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): blade bright green to yellowish green; Wikipedia: green, against the grey-green of the shrubs around it. sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.leaf_posture.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: fleshy linear leaves spreading from the stem; no source read says.

traits.stipules.note: German Wikipedia, 'Sarcobatus' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): no stipules.

traits.sexual_system.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): some authors say monoecious, others generally monoecious but occasionally dioecious; FNA genus: monoecious.

traits.inflorescence.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): staminate flowers in catkin-like spikes, small conelike structures at the ends of the smaller branches; pistillate flowers singly in leaf axils below them.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): staminate spikes typically 11-40 mm.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): staminate spike of 10-40 spirally arranged flowers.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): pistillate flowers and staminate spikes mostly on long lateral branches with 3-9 readily visible internodes.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): anthers (1-)2-4(-5).

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): stigmas 2.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): fruits achenes.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): fruits 3-5 mm, tapered at ends; FEIS 4-5 mm long.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): wing 0.7-1.4 cm diam; FEIS: about 1 cm wide including the wing.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: a dry, papery, veiny wing, pale tan when ripe; FNA says the wing is sometimes red-tinged but names no base colour.

traits.fruit_colour_ripening.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: green, fleshy perianth-wing while young, sometimes red-tinged (FNA); no source names the base colour.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=129190, read 2026-10-19): perianth accrescent, flaring to form a wing in fruit.

traits.fruit_persistence.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): maturation may extend over winter, with a few fruits left on the plant in early summer of the following year; dispersal late fall to early winter.

traits.flowering_months.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): flowering as early as May and as late as August; staminate flowers form mid-May, shed pollen early June, pistillate flowers evident early to mid-July. FNA: spring-summer.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): seed set mid-August, matures September to November; FNA: fruiting summer-early fall.

traits.leaf_out_months.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): bud burst generally late March to early April, as early as late February.

traits.leaf_fall_months.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): drops its leaves in fall and early winter.

traits.root_depth_max_m.note: Anderson, M. D. 2004, Sarcobatus vermiculatus, USFS Fire Effects Information System (read 2026-10-19): roots reported to 20 feet (6 m) deep; an excavated 1.8 m shrub had roots 5.5 m deep. FNA repeats a claim of taproots to 57 feet (17 m), not used.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): 600-2400 m; FEIS 152-2438 m.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): 600-2400 m.

traits.light.note: English Wikipedia, 'Sarcobatus' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): usually found in sunny, flat areas around playas.

traits.moisture.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): semiarid or arid plains, alkali flats, dry washes; a phreatophyte over shallow groundwater.

traits.soil_texture.note: English Wikipedia, 'Sarcobatus' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): most common on fine-grained soils in areas with a relatively high water table; FEIS adds sandy soil in the northeast of its range.

traits.habitat_notes.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): alkaline or saline soils in semiarid or arid plains, alkali flats, slopes, desert-shrub communities, sagebrush, saltflats, roadsides, dry washes, 600-2400 m; often in pure stands, especially in the Great Basin.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (read 2026-10-19): staminate flowers without a perianth, pistillate ones with a cup-shaped perianth that grows into the fruit's wing; drawn as the pistillate flower's tepals, since a plant draws one perianth.

traits.leaf_succulence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (read 2026-10-19): leaves sessile, succulent, linear.

traits.leaf_cross_section.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus (read 2026-10-19): leaves nearly round to somewhat flattened in section.

traits.fruit_seed_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Sarcobatus vermiculatus (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=242415620, read 2026-10-19): seeds 1.8-2.1 mm.
